panels.title: Active rooms
panels.description: Calls open on the media server right now. 0 outside a test is normal.

panels.title: People in calls now
panels.description: Participants connected to the media server right now. Each test room holds one sender and one viewer.

panels.title: Streams flowing
panels.description: Video or audio streams being sent into the media server right now. Lower than the number of senders means someone's camera is not arriving.

panels.title: Sessions created (5 min)
panels.description: Calls set up through the Dafter API in the last five minutes.

panels.title: Call join success (5 min)
panels.description: Of the people who tried to enter a call in the last five minutes, the share whose media connected. Below 99% is worth a look; below 95% people are failing to get in.

panels.title: Slowest API requests (p95)
panels.description: 95 out of 100 API requests in the last five minutes finished within this time. Under 100 ms is healthy; over 500 ms people notice.

panels.title: Packet loss (1 min)
panels.description: Share of media packets that did not arrive, averaged over the last minute. Under 1% is unnoticeable; over 5% video freezes.

panels.title: SFU CPU
panels.description: Processor used by the media server, where 100% is one full core. Over 70% is getting busy; over 90% calls start to degrade.

panels.title: Sessions created per minute
panels.description: Calls set up through the Dafter API each minute. Flat at 0 outside a test is normal.

panels.title: People joining per minute
panels.description: Join requests the Dafter API accepted each minute (one per participant entering a call).

panels.title: How long a request takes (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Time the Dafter API takes to answer. p50 is the typical request, p99 the slowest 1 in 100. Under 100 ms is healthy; over 500 ms people notice.

panels.title: Requests per minute by outcome
panels.description: API requests each minute, coloured by outcome: green succeeded, amber were rejected as invalid, red failed inside the service. Any red is a problem.

panels.title: Failed requests per minute by reason
panels.description: Requests the Dafter API could not serve, per minute, by reason. 0 is the only good value.

panels.title: Session setup and join time (p95)
panels.description: How long the two call-setup steps take inside the service, slowest 5% excluded. Setup writes the session record; join mints a token.

panels.title: Active rooms and people in calls
panels.description: Calls open on the media server and participants inside them. In a test, people = rooms x participants per room.

panels.title: Streams published and subscribed
panels.description: Media streams sent into the server (published) and delivered out to viewers (subscribed). Subscribed below published means viewers are not receiving.

panels.title: Packet loss
panels.description: Share of media packets lost, averaged per minute: incoming is sender to server, outgoing is server to viewer. Under 1% is unnoticeable; over 5% video freezes.

panels.title: Bandwidth in / out
panels.description: Media traffic into the server (incoming, from senders) and out of it (outgoing, to viewers), plus what had to be re-sent after loss.

panels.title: Round-trip time
panels.description: Average network round trip between the server and participants, per minute. Under 50 ms is local; over 300 ms conversations lag.

panels.title: Jitter
panels.description: Average variation in packet arrival time, per minute. Under 30 ms is smooth; over 100 ms audio and video stutter.

panels.title: Fresh-frame requests per minute
panels.description: Times per minute a receiver asked for a fresh video frame (PLI) after losing one: incoming from viewers, outgoing from the server to senders. A steady trickle is normal; a surge means loss. LiveKit does not export NACK counts.

panels.title: SFU CPU
panels.description: Processor used by the media server; 100% is one full core. Over 70% is getting busy; over 90% calls degrade.

panels.title: SFU memory
panels.description: Memory held by the media server process. It grows with participants and should fall back when calls end.

panels.title: People entering calls per minute
panels.description: Participants who started connecting to the media server and those whose media actually connected, per minute. The two lines should match.

panels.title: API requests per second (make loadtest)
panels.description: Total Dafter API requests per second. The HTTP load test drives hundreds; outside it this is near 0.

panels.title: Session setup time (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Time to create a session inside the service during the HTTP load test. This is the slow step: creates are written to a single SQLite file.

panels.title: Media packets per second in / out (make loadtest-media)
panels.description: Packets the media server receives from senders and sends to viewers each second. Scales with rooms x streams; a plateau while rooms still climb means the server or the network is saturated.

panels.title: Media connections fully established per minute
panels.description: Publisher and subscriber connections that completed the whole handshake each minute. During a ramp step this should equal the participants launched.

panels.title: Time to join a call (p95)
panels.description: How long a participant waits between asking to join and being connected to the media server, slowest 5% excluded.

panels.title: Call quality score
panels.description: LiveKit's own 1 (bad) to 5 (excellent) rating of each connection, averaged per minute.
